rounds.text: Intrasoft Technologies Ltd trades at a highly attractive relative valuation, offering a price-to-earnings ratio of 9.72x against a sector benchmark of 41.58x and a price-to-book ratio of 0.48x compared to a sector benchmark of 7.05x [E6, E7]. The business also trades at an EV/EBITDA of 8.26x versus the sector benchmark of 13.56x, and a modest price-to-book value of 0.91x [E2, E11]. Operational momentum shows clear signs of improvement, evidenced by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 24%, 3-year compounded profit growth of 91%, and trailing twelve-month profit growth of 41% [E16, E20, E21]. Furthermore, the yearly operating-margin trend has been increasing over the last 4 years, jumping to 24% in March 2026 from -38% three years earlier [E30, E32]. This fundamental turnaround is supported by a strong macroeconomic backdrop, as the Consumer Services sector sits in a verified tailwind with a tailwind score of +0.83 [E75]. Finally, the company maintains a conservatively financed balance sheet with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.15x as of March 2026 [E38]. Conceded: [E1, E8, E9, E10, E12, E13, E14, E18, E19, E22, E23, E24, E25, E34, E35, E36, E37, E39, E41, E45, E46, E47, E50, E51, E52, E53, E54, E55, E61, E62, E63, E64, E69, E70, E71, E72, E73].

The bull points to seemingly low relative valuation multiples such as a 9.72x P/E and 0.48x P/B [E6, E7], but this ignores the reported P/E of 141x [E1] and the stark reality that a discounted cash flow model values the stock at just Rs 6 against a market price of Rs 77.8 [E45], creating an extreme margin of safety of -1170.0% [E46]. Conceded: [E2, E11]. While the bull highlights short-term growth metrics like 3-year profit compounding [E20], these figures mask a terrible 10-year and 5-year compounded profit decline of -23% [E18, E19] and a 10-year sales contraction of -8% [E14]. Although the yearly operating margin expanded to 24% [E30], quarterly operating margins collapsed by 22 percentage points to 8% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], and earnings are artificially propped up by Rs 1.54 Cr in other income [E62]. The bull claims a fundamental turnaround under a sector tailwind [E75], but the company suffers from a crippling 349-day debtor cycle [E63], negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.34 Cr [E35], and a cash conversion ratio of -1.49x [E34]. Furthermore, promoter holding has steadily dropped by 4.62 percentage points [E41], annualised volatility sits high at 58.8% [E54], and the rules-based screen firmly scores the stock a 32 out of 100 with a high-confidence SELL rating [E65].
